<a id="page-hardware"></a>

## About this page

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Adds a security key as a way in: a password you choose that opens the vault only with the key plugged in and touched.

#### Why it is there

A password can be watched, guessed or phished. A key cannot be copied, so someone who learns the password still needs the key in their hand.

#### How it works

Choose the kind of key, give it a name, and choose the password that goes with it. It can be your master password, or a new one used only with the key.

Then plug in the key and touch it when asked. The vault saves a new way in that needs both. Next time, type that password at the door and touch the key when asked.

The key never hands over its secret. It answers a challenge stored in the vault, and its answer joins the password in unlocking the vault's key.

#### Limits

Ways in you already have still open the vault without the key. For the key to be needed, remove them under [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods), once you have a second key or another way in kept somewhere safe.

Lose the key and this way in is gone.

WM Pass does not ask for a key's PIN, so a key with a PIN set may refuse.

It guards the door, not an open vault. Once the vault is unlocked, the key plays no further part.

#### On Android

Choose the kind of key, give it a name, and choose the password that goes with it. It can be your master password, or a new one used only with the key.

Then hold the key to the back of the phone, or plug it in and touch it, and keep it there until the phone buzzes. The vault saves a new way in that needs both. Next time, type that password at the door and tap the key when asked.

The key never hands over its secret. It answers a challenge stored in the vault, and its answer joins the password in unlocking the vault's key.

See also [Add a security key](/guide/settings/security/#action-add-security-key), [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods), [The master password](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-master-password), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking).

<a id="action-hardware-fido2"></a>

## A FIDO2 security key

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Sets up a FIDO2 key, such as a YubiKey 5, a SoloKey or a Nitrokey, by USB.

#### How it works

WM Pass makes a new credential on the key that uses its hmac-secret extension. A key without hmac-secret cannot be used this way.

#### Limits

On Windows, only administrators can reach a FIDO2 key directly. Run WM Pass as administrator, or use a YubiKey with challenge-response instead.

#### On Android

Sets up a FIDO2 key, such as a YubiKey 5, a SoloKey or a Nitrokey, by NFC or USB.

See also [Hardware key](/guide/settings/hardware/), [A YubiKey with challenge-response](/guide/settings/hardware/#action-hardware-yubikey).

<a id="action-hardware-yubikey"></a>

## A YubiKey with challenge-response

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Sets up a YubiKey through its challenge-response feature in slot 2, instead of FIDO2.

#### How it works

Slot 2 has to be set up for challenge-response beforehand, in Yubico's own tool. WM Pass then stores a challenge in the vault, and the key's answer to it joins your password.

#### When to use it

For a YubiKey whose slot 2 you have already set up this way, or on Windows, where a FIDO2 key would need WM Pass to run as administrator.

See also [Hardware key](/guide/settings/hardware/), [A FIDO2 security key](/guide/settings/hardware/#action-hardware-fido2).
